tagline: Up out of the swamp to strawberry country, and back down.
intro: From Sorrento the byway heads north through small communities where fishing, hunting and trapping are still a way of life, and climbs to higher ground between Springfield and Ponchatoula, often called the Strawberry Capital of the World. Then old US 51 turns south across the Manchac swamp to Manchac on Lake Maurepas, where people come from all around for the catfish at Middendorf's, and runs about 17 more miles to LaPlace.

Springfield goes back to the 18th century, when it grew up at about the head of navigation on the Natalbany River, and bricks from an old Spanish fort can still be found about 200 yards in front of the post office.

moments.title: Tickfaw State Park
moments.text: West of Springfield, trails and more than a mile of boardwalk go through cypress-tupelo swamp and bottomland hardwoods to the Tickfaw River, where canoes are for rent.

moments.title: Joyce Wildlife Management Area
moments.text: South of Ponchatoula a boardwalk leads out into the swamp, and the tract takes in 100 acres of old Ponchatoula cypress that a 1950s mayor kept from the clear-cutters.

moments.title: Frenier
moments.text: Frenier has been a ghost town since the hurricane of 1915, which by legend struck during the funeral of Julia Brown, who had sung that when she died she would take the whole town.
